title: Integral integration of a divided-power sl2 module
statement:
Let $L$ be a free abelian group of finite rank [def-weil-pbc-free-module], $W=L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, and $E,F,H\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf Q}(W)$ satisfy $[H,E]=2E$, $[H,F]=-2F$, and $[E,F]=H$, where $[A,B]=AB-BA$. Suppose $E,F$ are nilpotent, $H$ is diagonalizable with integer eigenvalues, $L=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}(L\cap W_j)$ for $W_j=\ker(H-j)$, and $E^m/m!$ and $F^m/m!$ preserve $L$ for every integer $m\geq0$. Put $X_+(a)=\sum_m(E^m/m!)a^m$, $X_-(a)=\sum_m(F^m/m!)a^m$ and let $D(s)$ act by $s^j$ on $(L\cap W_j)\otimes A$. These finite polynomial formulas define, for every commutative ring $A$, automorphisms of $L\otimes A$. There is a unique homomorphism of affine group schemes over $\mathbf Z$,
$$v:\operatorname{SL}_{2,\mathbf Z}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(L),\qquad v(I+aE_{12})=X_+(a),\quad v(I+aE_{21})=X_-(a),\quad v(\operatorname{diag}(s,s^{-1}))=D(s).$$
Here $\operatorname{SL}_{2,\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[a,b,c,d]/(ad-bc-1)$ with matrix multiplication, and $\operatorname{GL}(L)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(L\otimes A)$; $E_{ij}$ denotes the matrix unit. A homomorphism of these affine group schemes is a natural family of group homomorphisms represented by a map of their coordinate rings. The formulas and uniqueness hold after every base change from $\mathbf Z$, including nonreduced rings. Rank zero and the trivial representation are allowed.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), pp.509--510, and characteristic-zero integration Theorem 23.70, pp.507--508. Agent-formulated integral sl2 input filling the omitted rank-one verification in Theorem 23.72; the lattice integration assertion is not explicitly proved in Milne.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sl2-rational-polynomial-model] to $W,E,F,H$. On each $P_n$ let $g=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ act by $P(X,Y)\mapsto P(aX+cY,bX+dY)$. Substitution gives $S_gS_h=S_{gh}$ and inverse $S_{g^{-1}}$; its matrix entries are homogeneous polynomials in $a,b,c,d$. Conjugate their direct sum by $T$ to obtain a morphism $\rho_{\mathbf Q}:\operatorname{SL}_{2,\mathbf Q}\to\operatorname{GL}(W)$. For $x_+(t)=I+tE_{12}$, substitution is $P(X,Y+tX)=\sum_m t^m e_n^mP/m!$; for $x_-(t)$ it is $P(X+tY,Y)=\sum_m t^m f_n^mP/m!$. The diagonal acts on $X^{n-i}Y^i$ by $s^{n-2i}$. The intertwining identities therefore identify these restrictions of $\rho_{\mathbf Q}$ with exactly $X_+(t),X_-(t),D(s)$ on $W$. This constructs the rational action without assuming an integral action.

source.place: Theorem 23.70, pp.507-508, and Example 22.33, p.472; agent construction of the rational action from the explicit polynomial models.

proof.text: Fix any finite basis of $L$. The divided powers have integral matrices by hypothesis and vanish for sufficiently large $m$. Expanding in commuting variables gives $X_\pm(t)X_\pm(u)=X_\pm(t+u)$: the coefficient identity is $(E^r/r!)(E^q/q!)=\binom{r+q}{r}E^{r+q}/(r+q)!$, and likewise for $F$. These are identities of integral matrices, since they hold in the containing rational matrix algebra. Thus $X_\pm(t)^{-1}=X_\pm(-t)$ over every ring. The finitely many weight projections $p_j:L\to L\cap W_j\hookrightarrow L$ supplied by the assumed direct sum satisfy $\sum_jp_j=1$ and $p_jp_k=\delta_{jk}p_j$. Hence $D(s)=\sum_js^jp_j$ is an integral Laurent polynomial matrix and $D(s)D(s^{-1})=1$. No choice of bases of the weight summands is needed. Set $N=X_+(1)X_-(-1)X_+(1)$, an integral invertible matrix.

source.place: Equation (153), p.510; agent binomial and weight-projection verification over the universal polynomial rings.

proof.text:
Put $G=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R=\mathbf Z[a,b,c,d]/(ad-bc-1)$. The opens $U_a=D(a)$ and $U_c=D(c)$ cover $G$, since $ad-bc=1$. Their rings are $R_a=\mathbf Z[a,a^{-1},b,c]$ (eliminate $d$) and $R_c=\mathbf Z[c,c^{-1},a,d]$ (eliminate $b$). For the universal matrix $g$ on these opens, direct multiplication gives
$$g=x_-(c/a)\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1})x_+(b/a)\quad\text{on }U_a,$$
$$g=w\,x_-(-a/c)\operatorname{diag}(-c,(-c)^{-1})x_+(d/c)\quad\text{on }U_c,$$
where $w=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)=x_+(1)x_-(-1)x_+(1)$. Define morphisms into $\operatorname{GL}(L)$ on these charts by
$$V_a=X_-(c/a)D(a)X_+(b/a),\qquad V_c=N X_-(-a/c)D(-c)X_+(d/c).$$
All factors and their inverses are matrices over the displayed chart rings by step 2, so these are actual morphisms, not just maps on field-valued points.

source.place: Agent two-chart construction supplementing equation (153), pp.509-510; all factorizations are explicit 2 by 2 matrix identities.

proof.text: Over $\mathbf Q$, both $V_a$ and $V_c$ equal the restriction of the action from step 1, by its root and torus formulas and the factorizations in step 3. On $U_a\cap U_c$ the coordinate ring is $\mathbf Z[a,a^{-1},b,c,c^{-1}]$. Its map into its rationalization is injective: expand any Laurent polynomial in its distinct monomials, whose integer coefficients embed in $\mathbf Q$. Consequently every entry of $V_a-V_c$ is zero already over this integral overlap ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to the two open charts to obtain a unique morphism $v:G\to\operatorname{GL}(L)$ restricting to them; its rational base change is $\rho_{\mathbf Q}$.

source.place: Agent gluing of the integral formulas; the gluing theorem cited in the DAG is Stacks Tags 01JA, 01JJ, 04TN and 00AN (mapping-property-glue).

proof.text: Compare the morphisms $v\circ m$ and $m_{\operatorname{GL}}\circ(v\times v)$ on $G\times_{\mathbf Z}G$. The four products $U_\epsilon\times U_\eta$, $\epsilon,\eta\in\{a,c\}$, form an open cover. Each coordinate ring is a Laurent polynomial ring over $\mathbf Z$ in two independent triples of chart coordinates, so injects into its rationalization by the same coefficient argument. The difference of the two matrix entries becomes zero there because $\rho_{\mathbf Q}$ is a homomorphism; hence every difference was zero integrally. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives the multiplication identity globally. At the identity the $U_a$ formula is $X_-(0)D(1)X_+(0)=1$. These two identities make $v$ a group-scheme homomorphism (and force preservation of inverses).

source.place: Agent verification of the group law over the four universal integral product charts; comparison with Theorem 23.70 on their rationalizations.

proof.text: The upper root subgroup and diagonal torus lie in $U_a$ with coordinates $(a,b,c)=(1,t,0)$ and $(s,0,0)$, respectively; the lower root subgroup also lies in $U_a$, with $(a,b,c)=(1,0,t)$. Thus the $V_a$ formula gives all three prescribed restrictions. After any base change $\mathbf Z\to B$, the same two opens cover $G_B$, and the two factorizations still hold over their universal coordinate rings. Any $B$-group-scheme homomorphism with the prescribed restrictions must send $w=x_+(1)x_-(-1)x_+(1)$ to $N_B$, so those factorizations force its chart formulas to be $(V_a)_B$ and $(V_c)_B$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] proves it equals $v_B$. The construction uses integral coordinate identities, hence applies to every commutative $B$-algebra, including nonreduced ones. For rank zero the matrices are the unique automorphism of the zero module; trivial summands give identity matrices throughout.

source.place: Agent restriction and universal-base-change uniqueness argument, completing the integral rank-one input to equation (153).
